migration_steps.activity: Establish PQC migration programme governance: appoint an accountable owner, define scope covering the four cryptographic assets, agree risk appetite for harvest-now-decrypt-later exposure, and set up a cross-functional working group including cryptography, infrastructure, applications, HSM operations, procurement, legal/compliance, and the core banking platform owner.
prerequisites: Executive sponsorship and named programme owner
Approved first-phase budget of USD 250,000
Access to current architecture and cryptographic inventory records

migration_steps.activity: Perform a complete cryptographic inventory and data-flow mapping: enumerate all RSA-2048 TLS certificates, ECDSA P-256 internal API authentication keys, RSA-3072 key-wrapping keys protecting database encryption keys, and ECDH P-256 internal secure channels. Record key owners, certificate expiry dates, data classification, data retention periods, and whether each asset protects data with a confidentiality lifetime of 10 to 15 years.
prerequisites: Programme governance established (step 1)
Read access to certificate stores, HSM key inventory, API gateway configuration, and database encryption key metadata
Data classification and retention schedule from data owners

migration_steps.activity: Conduct a quantum risk assessment and prioritisation: classify each asset by harvest-now-decrypt-later exposure based on data confidentiality lifetime, classify ML-KEM as the target for key establishment and ML-DSA as the target for digital signatures, and rank assets. Prioritise RSA-3072 key wrapping protecting long-lived database encryption keys and ECDH P-256 channels carrying long-lived sensitive data first, because traffic or wrapped keys captured today could be decrypted once a cryptographically relevant quantum computer exists.
prerequisites: Completed cryptographic inventory (step 2)
Agreed data retention and confidentiality periods
Documented risk appetite from step 1

migration_steps.activity: Engage the Thales Luna Network HSM 7 vendor in writing to obtain confirmed production support status, firmware compatibility matrix, certification status, and delivery timeline for ML-KEM and ML-DSA. Do not treat any roadmap statement as confirmed capability until written evidence is received.
prerequisites: Programme governance established (step 1)
Current HSM model, firmware version, and support contract details available

migration_steps.activity: Engage the third-party core banking platform vendor in writing to obtain a PQC compatibility statement, supported cryptographic libraries, migration roadmap, and any contractual constraints on cryptographic changes. Request written confirmation before any production dependency is assumed.
prerequisites: Programme governance established (step 1)
Current core banking platform version and contract details available

migration_steps.activity: Define target PQC architecture and hybrid transition strategy: specify ML-KEM for key establishment (including hybrid X25519/ML-KEM or ECDH/ML-KEM where supported) and ML-DSA for digital signatures (including hybrid ECDSA/ML-DSA where supported). Document crypto-agility requirements, key lifecycle changes, certificate profile changes, and fallback behaviour. Do not commit to production designs that depend on unconfirmed HSM or core banking capabilities.
prerequisites: Risk assessment and prioritisation complete (step 3)
Initial written responses from HSM and core banking vendors (steps 4 and 5)
Regulatory and compliance review of cryptographic change obligations

migration_steps.activity: Procure non-production laboratory capability for PQC testing: software cryptographic libraries supporting ML-KEM and ML-DSA, test certificates, and a non-production HSM or HSM simulator only if the vendor confirms availability and compatibility in writing. Budget allocation must remain within the USD 250,000 first-phase limit.
prerequisites: Target architecture defined (step 6)
Written vendor confirmation of non-production compatibility
Procurement approval within first-phase budget

migration_steps.activity: Build and run non-production laboratory tests: validate ML-KEM key establishment and ML-DSA signature operations in software, test hybrid modes, measure performance and interoperability, and test TLS and API authentication flows in a lab environment. Do not perform production cryptographic changes or HSM firmware upgrades.
prerequisites: Laboratory capability procured (step 7)
Target architecture and test plan approved (step 6)
Non-production environment available and permitted by internal policy

migration_steps.activity: Prepare production migration runbooks, rollback plans, change records, and regulatory notifications for the first production PQC changes, scheduled only after the change freeze ends on 15 January 2027 and only for assets whose HSM and core banking dependencies are confirmed in writing.
prerequisites: Laboratory testing results accepted (step 8)
Written HSM and core banking confirmations for the specific assets in scope
Operational approval and change advisory board scheduling after the freeze

migration_steps.activity: Execute first production cryptographic change after the change freeze: migrate the highest-priority long-lived data protection asset that has confirmed vendor support, using hybrid ML-KEM key establishment where the HSM and platform support it in writing. If no written confirmation exists, defer this step and continue planning and lab work only.
prerequisites: Change freeze ended (15 January 2027 inclusive)
Written HSM vendor confirmation of production ML-KEM support and firmware compatibility
Written core banking vendor confirmation where the asset depends on that platform
Approved change record, rollback plan, and operational approval
Successful laboratory validation (step 8)

migration_steps.activity: Plan and schedule HSM firmware upgrade to a PQC-capable release only after the vendor provides written confirmation of production support, compatibility, certification, and a delivery timeline. The upgrade must occur outside the change freeze and after operational approval.
prerequisites: Written Thales confirmation of PQC-capable firmware release and production support
Compatibility validation in non-production laboratory
Change freeze ended and operational approval obtained
Rollback and recovery plan approved

migration_steps.activity: Deploy major application changes for ML-DSA digital signatures in internal API authentication and for ML-KEM key establishment in internal secure channels, only after core banking vendor written confirmation and HSM production support are obtained and validated.
prerequisites: Written core banking vendor PQC compatibility confirmation
Written HSM production support confirmation for ML-DSA and ML-KEM
Successful laboratory and pilot validation
Change freeze ended and operational approval obtained

blockers.blocker: Thales Luna Network HSM 7 production support, firmware compatibility, certification status, and delivery timeline for ML-KEM and ML-DSA are unconfirmed.
blockers.reason: Production PQC key establishment and digital signature operations that rely on HSM-protected keys cannot be safely deployed without confirmed firmware support and compatibility. Assuming support would risk service availability and regulatory non-compliance.
blockers.resolution_required: Obtain written confirmation from Thales of production support, firmware version compatibility, certification status, and delivery timeline for ML-KEM and ML-DSA, followed by non-production validation.

blockers.blocker: Third-party core banking platform vendor has not provided written confirmation of PQC compatibility or a migration roadmap.
blockers.reason: Cryptographic changes in applications that depend on the core banking platform cannot be validated or deployed without vendor confirmation. The bank cannot assume compatibility or modify vendor-controlled components.
blockers.resolution_required: Obtain written PQC compatibility statement, supported cryptographic libraries, migration roadmap, and contractual constraints from the core banking vendor.

blockers.blocker: PQC-capable non-production HSM or HSM simulator availability and cost are unconfirmed.
blockers.reason: Laboratory testing of HSM-backed ML-KEM and ML-DSA operations requires compatible non-production hardware or simulation. Without it, HSM-dependent migration steps cannot be validated within budget.
blockers.resolution_required: Confirm availability, compatibility, and cost of non-production HSM capability with the vendor and complete procurement within the USD 250,000 first-phase budget.

blockers.blocker: Interoperability and performance of hybrid ML-KEM and ML-DSA modes across TLS, API authentication, and database key wrapping are unvalidated in the bank's environment.
blockers.reason: Hybrid and PQC algorithms may affect latency, certificate sizes, protocol negotiation, and application behaviour. Production changes cannot proceed without laboratory validation.
blockers.resolution_required: Complete non-production laboratory testing and performance benchmarking, and document accepted results before production scheduling.

blockers.blocker: Regulatory notification and approval requirements for cryptographic changes affecting customer data protection are not yet confirmed.
blockers.reason: Banking regulators may require notification or approval before changes to cryptographic controls protecting sensitive customer information. Proceeding without confirmation risks non-compliance.
blockers.resolution_required: Obtain legal and compliance confirmation of notification and approval obligations, and complete any required regulatory engagement before production changes.

blockers.blocker: Production change freeze from 1 December 2026 through 15 January 2027 inclusive prohibits production cryptographic changes, HSM firmware upgrades, and major application deployments.
blockers.reason: No production migration activity can be scheduled during the freeze. Only planning, documentation, vendor engagement, and permitted non-production laboratory activities may continue.
blockers.resolution_required: Schedule all production changes after 15 January 2027 and obtain operational approval and change advisory board approval for post-freeze windows.

vendor_dependencies.evidence_required: Written confirmation of production support, firmware compatibility matrix, certification status, and delivery timeline for ML-KEM and ML-DSA, plus non-production validation results.
Written PQC compatibility statement, supported cryptographic libraries, migration roadmap, and contractual constraints on cryptographic changes.

cost_assumptions: Programme management and governance: USD 35,000 for internal and contracted programme staff over the first phase.
Cryptographic inventory and data-flow mapping: USD 30,000 for tooling, contractor support, and data owner workshops.
Risk assessment and architecture planning: USD 25,000 for specialist cryptography consultancy and compliance review.
Vendor engagement and contractual review: USD 15,000 for legal, procurement, and technical liaison effort.
Non-production laboratory capability: USD 60,000 for software PQC libraries, test certificates, and non-production HSM or simulator only if confirmed available and compatible.
Laboratory testing and validation: USD 45,000 for engineering effort, performance testing, and interoperability validation.
Production runbooks, change preparation, and regulatory engagement: USD 25,000 for documentation, change management, and compliance support.
Contingency: USD 0 allocated within the estimate; the USD 15,000 headroom below the USD 250,000 limit is retained as unallocated reserve and is not committed.

No production HSM firmware upgrade or major application deployment costs are included in the first-phase estimate because those activities are blocked pending written vendor confirmation and are scheduled after the change freeze.
